sent:
Milo —

We checked sundriftdrinks.example: it’s returning 502. If you run paid, every click burns. Here’s the prioritised fix you can ship today:

1) Resilience first
- Turn on multi‑region uptime monitoring with instant alerts.
- Front the site with a CDN/WAF and sanity‑check DNS; separate a lightweight fallback page on a different host/subdomain so it stays up even if the main app falls over.

2) Fallback landing page (one ad, one promise, one page)
- Hero: the launch promise, pack visual, primary CTA to buy (or waitlist if checkout isn’t ready).
- Social proof: 2–3 tight proof points (press/early testers).
- FAQs: ingredients, pack size, delivery/returns, who it’s for.
- Single path to checkout; no header nav or side exits.

3) Pre‑launch QA (mobile first)
- Full add‑to‑cart → checkout → confirmation flow, including promo codes, shipping, taxes, OOS states, and graceful 404/500 fallbacks.
- Validate that purchase events fire once and reconcile with orders in your analytics and ad platforms.
- Trigger post‑purchase comms off an order; test transactional emails/SMS.
- Basic speed passes on the fallback page and images; compress and lazy‑load below the fold.

4) Offer‑to‑page alignment for a January drinks launch
- Build around one campaign idea that sells an occasion (wellness reset, sociability, focus) rather than ingredients; run variants of the same idea across channels.
- If you’re in functional/alt/premium RTD, plan a subscribe‑and‑save or loyalty hook from day one; repeat is the margin.
- Don’t send ads to the homepage. Oatside Kitchen cut first‑order CPA 38% by moving to three offer pages; same play here.

We don’t guarantee ROAS; we work in 90‑day blocks so you can stop if results aren’t there. If you want, we can turn this into a one‑page pre‑launch checklist you can drop into a sprint board.
